name: Sindhi Script
basis: calligram: words sized and weighted by tone, set right to left (how)
note: Typography in a browser font; no pen modelled.

lumenary.blurb: Your picture written out in Sindhi, right to left. Words and letters grow and thicken where the light is strong, so the page reads as a calligraphic portrait.

facts.era: Standardised in 1853, with a poetry tradition far older
facts.bestOn: Portraits and pictures with bright, clear shapes

why: Sindhi is written in the Arabic script with letters of its own, for sounds that Arabic does not have: ٻ ڀ ٽ ٿ ڄ ڃ ڇ ڌ ڏ ڙ ڪ ڳ ڱ ڻ and others. The letters join, and each takes a different shape at the start, the middle and the end of a word. This treatment sets words in rows, right to left, and lets your picture decide how large and heavy each word is, so the page reads as a calligraphic portrait.
how: Give each word to the browser, which shapes and joins it with the Noto Naskh Arabic font, and set the text right to left.
Give each line a pitch of 1.45 times the letter size and fill it from the right, one word after another, with a gap of 0.32 to 0.42 of the font size.
Measure each word at the base size and read the tone v of the picture at its middle (the brightness on a dark page, the darkness on a cream one).
Set the size again from v, and make the word bold where v is above 0.45.
Colour the words from the picture, in gold, or in plain ink.
history: In 1853 the British administration adopted an Arabic-based alphabet of 52 letters for Sindhi, after a period in which several scripts were in use. Sindhi is also written in Devanagari in India. The language carries a great poetic tradition, notably Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai in the eighteenth century, whose verses are still sung at his shrine. The built-in word list here was drafted without a native proofread, so treat its spelling as provisional.
uses: Portrait gifts with a name or poem
terms: A clear, rounded style of Arabic script, good for reading.
The different shapes a letter takes at the start, middle or end of a word.
The direction in which Arabic-script languages are written.
paragraphs: Sindhi is written in the Arabic script with extra letters of its own, for sounds that Arabic does not have: ٻ ڀ ٽ ٿ ڄ ڃ ڇ ڌ ڏ ڙ ڪ ڳ ڱ ڻ and others. The letters join, and each takes a different shape at the start, the middle and the end of a word. The program does not do the joining itself; it gives each word to the browser, which shapes it with the Noto Naskh Arabic font, and sets the text right to left. The word list is short and is made of everyday words: Sindh, the Indus, love, peace, earth, light, a friend, language, book, water, sun, moon, art, poem, melody, knowledge, gift and lamp. It was drafted without a native proofread, so treat the spelling as provisional.

Each line has a pitch of 1.45 times the letter size. Words fill the line from the right, one after another, with a gap of 0.32 to 0.42 of the font size. The size of each word follows your picture: the program measures the word at the base size, reads the tone v of the picture at its middle (the brightness on a dark page, the darkness on a cream one) and sets the size again from v. The words are bold where v is above 0.45. Where the picture is bright, the words are large and heavy; where it is dark, small and thin. The page therefore reads as a calligraphic portrait.

equations.note: Font size from tone: s is the letter size and κ the “size follows light” slider. v = 0 gives half size at κ = 1, and v = 1 gives one and a half.
Setting a line from right to left. ξ is a random number per word.
Ink brightness also follows tone, so the bright areas are lit from within.

presets.text: Gold ink on an indigo page makes a festival poster.
Strong size following the light builds a clear portrait.
Letters mode shows the shapes of the alphabet itself.
